office.name: Kittitas County Board of County Commissioners, Office of the Chair
office.place: Kittitas County, Washington (county seat Ellensburg; board office in the Kittitas County Courthouse, 205 W. 5th Ave., Suite 108, Ellensburg, WA 98926)
office.board_office: 205 W. 5th Ave., Suite 108, Ellensburg, WA 98926; (509) 962-7508; Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m.
office.remit: A three-member board of county commissioners in a non-charter Washington county: the county's legislative and executive authority. It adopts the county budget and ordinances, approves contracts, and directly oversees the appointed departments: Public Works (county roads, bridges and Bowers Field airport), Solid Waste (two transfer stations and long-haul disposal), Community Development Services (building permits, land use and the fire marshal), the Kittitas Valley Event Center and County Fair, the Noxious Weed Control Board's program, Human Resources, IT and Maintenance. It funds but does not run the offices of independently elected officials (Sheriff, including the jail and emergency management; Prosecutor; Auditor; Treasurer; Assessor; Clerk; courts). Regular meetings the first and third Tuesdays at 9:00 a.m. in the Commissioners' Auditorium; study sessions with department heads most Mondays. The board elects its own chair. The county has no county administrator; the board office has three staff.

succession.rule: Washington Constitution Article II, Section 15: a vacancy in a partisan county elective office is filled by the board of county commissioners (for a commissioner vacancy, the remaining commissioners), choosing one of three persons nominated by the county central committee of the vacating officer's party, from the same commissioner district; if a majority does not agree within 60 days, the governor appoints from the same list within 30 days. The appointee holds office until a successor is elected at the next general election. Since July 27, 2025 this is the only method: chapter 133, Laws of 2025 (SB 5288) repealed the statutory alternative in RCW 36.32.070.
succession.election: RCW 42.12.040(1): if the vacancy occurs on or after the first day of the regular filing period (May 2026), except in the last year of the term, the successor is elected at the next succeeding general election. The District 2 term runs to Dec 31, 2028, so the vacancy of Sept 1, 2026 goes on the November 2027 ballot for the rest of the term.
succession.chair: The board elects its own chair. The previous District 2 commissioner was chair; the District 3 commissioner (vice chair) acted as chair Sept 1-21 and, being on the November 3, 2026 ballot, asked not to chair for the rest of the year; the District 1 commissioner declined; on Sept 21 the board elected Gustafsen chair for the remainder of 2026.
succession.timeline: Tue Sept 1: previous District 2 commissioner's resignation effective (no reason given anywhere). Thu Sept 10: the county central committee submits three nominees. Tue Sept 15: the two remaining commissioners appoint Gustafsen at the regular meeting, 2-0. Wed Sept 16, 8:30 a.m.: oath of office, Commissioners' Auditorium. Mon Sept 21: special meeting; board reorganizes and elects her chair, 3-0.
sources: Washington Constitution Art. II, Sec. 15 (text via codes.findlaw.com/wa/washington-constitution/wa-const-art-2-sect-15/ and leg.wa.gov constitution PDF; checked 2026-10-07)

how_the_office_works.staff_and_funding: Commissioners and the board office's three staff (clerk of the board, two office administrators) are paid from the county current expense (general) fund; there is no county administrator, so department heads report to the board, which assigns each commissioner liaison departments. Source: co.kittitas.wa.us/boc/about.aspx and departments.aspx.
how_the_office_works.approvals: The board approves contracts, leases above the department head's delegated authority, fee schedules (by resolution) and budget amendments; the annual budget is adopted after hearings in early December (RCW 36.40). Airport hangar leases at the standard rate are signed by the airport manager under delegated authority.
how_the_office_works.not_the_board: Emergency alerts and the jail are run by the elected Sheriff; the board only funds them. Scenarios avoid them.
